questions.text: Do you expect more demand for this cake?
Are ingredients for another batch available?
Is a qualified employee available without a higher-priority task?
How many minutes until a new batch would be ready to sell?

rules.explanation: At most one slice remains and further demand is expected, so another batch is needed.
Another batch is needed and ingredients and qualified staff are available, so preparation is feasible.
Preparation is feasible and there is enough selling time, so start another batch.
There is insufficient time to prepare and sell another batch before closing.
A batch is needed and time permits, but missing ingredients prevent preparation.
Ingredients and time are available, but no qualified employee is currently free.
At most one slice remains, so the preparation threshold is reached.
Preparation finishes before closing, leaving some time to sell the cake.
Preparation would finish at or after closing, leaving no selling time.
More than one slice remains, so the preparation threshold has not yet been reached.
No further demand is expected, so another batch is not needed.

recommendations.text: Start preparing the next cake batch now.
Do not start another batch before closing.
Review ingredient availability before preparing another batch.
Postpone preparation and reassess when qualified staff become available.
Enough cake remains for now under the one-slice threshold; reassess as slices sell.
No further batch is needed because no more demand is expected.
